literal: By benevolence comes ruin if it is said, that a person having sold acquiring worth it possesses.
translation: If ruin comes from doing one's duty to others, that ruin is worth a person selling himself to acquire.
modern: பிறருக்கு உதவுவதால் ஒருவனுக்குக் கேடு வரும் என்றால், அக்கேடு ஒருவன் தன்னை விற்றாவது வாங்கிக்கொள்ளும் தகுதியை உடையது.
explanation: The couplet explores the ultimate value of benevolence (ஒப்புரவு) by contrasting it with ruin (கேடு). It states that if helping others leads to one's own ruin or poverty, such a loss is actually a noble acquisition. The phrase 'விற்று கோள்' (selling to acquire) suggests that this kind of ruin is so honorable that a person should be willing to sell themselves or all they own just to obtain it. By using the language of commerce, the poet emphasizes that the moral worth of self-sacrifice far outweighs any material loss.
